overview: The classic eukaryotic cell comparison: shared organelles, but structural features unique to a stationary, photosynthetic lifestyle versus a mobile, heterotrophic one.
genZNote: Plants build a house. Animals just wear a jacket.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Eukaryotic cells with a rigid cell wall, a large central vacuole, and chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
aspects.valueB: Eukaryotic cells lacking a cell wall and chloroplasts, typically more flexible in shape.

aspects.label: Cell Wall
aspects.valueA: Present — rigid cellulose cell wall outside the plasma membrane.
aspects.valueB: Absent — only a flexible plasma membrane.

aspects.label: Chloroplasts / Photosynthesis
aspects.valueA: Present, enabling photosynthesis and self-generation of glucose.
aspects.valueB: Absent — animal cells are heterotrophic and obtain energy from ingested food.

aspects.label: Vacuole
aspects.valueA: Large, single central vacuole for turgor pressure, storage, and waste.
aspects.valueB: Small, multiple vacuoles if present, mainly for storage/transport.

aspects.label: Shape
aspects.valueA: Fixed, rectangular/regular shape due to the cell wall.
aspects.valueB: Irregular, flexible shape without a wall.

aspects.label: Centrioles
aspects.valueA: Typically absent in most plant cells.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Cell wall, chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole.
aspects.valueB: No cell wall or chloroplasts; has centrioles and flexible shape.
